definition_en: a person or team that has won a competition, or someone who publicly defends a person or cause
core_image: 站在领奖台最高处、把奖杯举过头顶的人
scene: 决赛终场哨响，全场观众起立欢呼。The young boxer became champion after twelve hard rounds.
sceneCN: 这里 champion 指「冠军」（第 1 个义项：比赛中击败所有对手的人）；句意是这位年轻拳手在十二个艰苦回合后成为冠军。

senses.title: The winner of a contest
senses.definition: a person or team that has defeated all rivals in a competition
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛中击败所有对手的个人或队伍
senses.example: She was champion three years running.
senses.exampleCN: 她连续三年夺得冠军。
senses.why: The Latin base named an open field, and the fighter who won there took the name of the ground.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词基指开阔的场地，在那里取胜的斗士便借用了场地的名字。

senses.title: A defender of a cause
senses.definition: a person who speaks or fights publicly for another person or for a principle
senses.definitionCN: 公开为他人或某种原则发声、抗争的人
senses.example: He became a champion of free speech.
senses.exampleCN: 他成了言论自由的捍卫者。
senses.why: The victor who fought for a helpless client lent the word its protecting sense.
senses.whyCN: 为无助者出战的胜者，把「保护」的含义借给了这个词。

senses.title: To support publicly
senses.definition: to defend or promote a person, idea or policy in public
senses.definitionCN: 在公开场合为某人、某观念或某政策辩护或推动
senses.example: The actor championed the small theatre for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 这位演员为那家小剧院呼吁了几十年。
senses.why: Once a person was called a champion of a cause, the noun naturally turned into a verb of support.
senses.whyCN: 当人被称作某项事业的 champion 之后，这个名词自然转化为表示支持的动词。

intro.en: Champion travelled from the Latin word for a field to the name of the fighter who stood on it.
intro.cn: champion 从拉丁语表示田野的词出发，最终指站在那片场地上决斗的人。

items.en: Campus meant an open field or plain.
items.cn: 拉丁语 campus 意为开阔的田野或平地。

items.en: Campio named the fighter who settled a dispute by single combat.
items.cn: campio 指以单打决斗解决争端的人。

items.en: Champion entered Old French with the tournament sense intact.
items.cn: champion 带着比武大会的含义进入古法语。

items.en: English used champion for a warrior who fought for another man in a trial.
items.cn: 十三世纪英语用 champion 指在审判中替人出战的武士。

items.en: The word now covers sports winners and public defenders of a cause.
items.cn: 如今该词涵盖体育冠军与公共事业的捍卫者。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the field root, while the meaning group names people who prevail.
note.cn: 形近组共享「场地」词根，近义组列出最终取胜的人。

entries.definition: an informal word for a champion
a contest held to decide the top player or team
entries.definitionCN: 决出最佳选手或队伍的比赛

entries.definition: the grounds of a school or college
a person who defeats an opponent
someone who comes first in a contest
a person who protects someone or something

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the field root, the short form champ and the fixed phrase champion of a cause.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「场地」词根、短词 champ 以及固定说法 champion of a cause。

normal.en: Champion keeps the field inside it: campus is the open ground where the duel was fought.
normal.cn: champion 里藏着「场地」：campus 就是当年决斗的开阔地。

normal.en: Shorten the word and you get champ, the shout aimed at a winner.
normal.cn: 把词缩短就得到 champ，正是观众对胜者喊出的短词。

normal.en: The -ion ending marks a person, so a champion is the one who owns the field.
normal.cn: -ion 结尾标记出人，champion 就是占住场地的那个人。

normal.en: A champion of a cause wins arguments rather than medals.
normal.cn: a champion of a cause 赢的是论辩，而不是奖牌。

normal.en: The verb champion takes a cause as its object, as in champion the poor.
normal.cn: 动词 champion 的宾语是事业，如 champion the poor 意为为穷人发声。

abstract.en: Picture a raised fist and a silver cup held above a cheering crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一只举起的拳头和一只被举过欢呼人群的银杯。

abstract.en: Picture a lone speaker defending a small village against a powerful company.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人独自为小村庄对抗一家大公司。

abstract.en: Picture a referee lifting the winner's arm at the end of a long fight.
abstract.cn: 想象漫长比赛结束时裁判举起胜者的手臂。

examples.en: She became champion at the age of nineteen.
examples.cn: 她十九岁就成为冠军。

examples.en: The champions lifted the cup together.
examples.cn: 冠军们一起举起了奖杯。

examples.en: He championed the rights of migrant workers.
examples.cn: 他为外来工的权利奔走呼吁。

dict_mnemonic.text: champion 里有 camp（营地）：在营地里比到最后的人，就是冠军。

root: 源自拉丁语 campus（田野、场地），经晚期拉丁语 campio（场上决斗者）与古法语 champion 进入英语；与 camp 同源。

sensesIntro.en: A fighter who wins on the field gives the contest sense, and a fighter who stands up for another gives the defending sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 在场上取胜的斗士给出比赛义，替他人出头的斗士给出捍卫义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fighter left standing on the open field.
core.cn: 核心意象：在开阔场地上站到最后的斗士。

branches.en: A cup and a medal mark the contest winner.
branches.cn: 奖杯与奖牌标记出比赛的胜者。

branches.en: The defender sense keeps the idea of fighting for someone.
branches.cn: 捍卫义保留为某人而战的意思。

branches.en: The verb champion turns the defence into an action.
branches.cn: 动词 champion 把这种捍卫变成动作。

branches.en: Both senses centre on a person who prevails.
branches.cn: 两个义项都以最终取胜的人为中心。

branches.en: Public support appears as both noun and verb.
branches.cn: 公开支持既作名词也作动词出现。

intro.en: Champion keeps the -camp- field root across noun, verb and derived forms.
intro.cn: champion 在名词、动词与派生形式之间保留 -camp- 场地词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin campus and campio are the field and the fighter that gave English the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 campus 与 campio 分别是给出英语这个词的场地与斗士。

items.example: The champion waved to the crowd.

items.exampleCN: 他们曾为这项新法律奔走。
她正在为乡村学校发声。

items.meaning: an informal word for a champion

latinEntries.example: Campio passed into French as champion.
latinEntries.exampleCN: campio 进入法语后写作 champion。

latinEntries.example: Campus gave the word its field image.
latinEntries.exampleCN: campus 赋予这个词场地意象。

definition_zh: 锦标赛；冠军称号；冠军地位
definition_en: a competition held to decide the best player or team, or the position of being a champion
core_image: 一块刻着赛事名字的金属奖牌
scene: 体育馆的记分牌一直亮到深夜。The championship drew teams from every province.
sceneCN: 这里 championship 指「锦标赛」（第 1 个义项：决定冠军归属的比赛）；句意是这项锦标赛吸引了各省的队伍。

pos.zh: 锦标赛；冠军称号；冠军地位

senses.title: A contest for the top title
senses.definition: a competition held to decide which player or team is the best
senses.definitionCN: 为决出最佳选手或队伍而举办的比赛
senses.example: The national championship starts on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 全国锦标赛周一开始。
senses.why: The suffix -ship turns the winner's name into the contest that produces a winner.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ship 把胜者的名字变成产出胜者的那场比赛。

senses.title: The status of being champion
senses.definition: the position or title of being a champion
senses.definitionCN: 身为冠军的身份或头衔
senses.example: She held the championship for five years.
senses.exampleCN: 她保持冠军称号达五年之久。
senses.why: The same suffix also names a state or rank, so the word can mean the title itself.
senses.whyCN: 同一个后缀也能表示状态或等级，因此这个词也可指头衔本身。

intro.en: Championship is champion plus the native noun suffix -ship, which names a state or an office.
intro.cn: championship 是 champion 加上本土名词后缀 -ship，该后缀表示状态或职位。

items.en: Campus meant an open field where contests were held.
items.cn: 拉丁语 campus 意为举行比赛的开阔场地。

items.en: Campio named the man who fought and won there.
items.cn: campio 指在那里作战并取胜的人。

items.en: The native suffix -scipe named a state, rank or office.
items.cn: 本土后缀 -scipe 表示状态、等级或职位。

items.en: Champion and -ship joined to name the standing of a victor.
items.cn: champion 与 -ship 结合，指胜者的地位。

items.en: The word now means both the contest and the title won in it.
items.cn: 如今该词既指比赛，也指在比赛中赢得的头衔。

note.en: The look-alike group builds on champion, while the meaning group lists other contests and honours.
note.cn: 形近组由 champion 构成，近义组列出其他赛事与荣誉。

entries.definition: a person who has won a contest
an informal word for a champion
the grounds of a school or college
a series of contests to decide a winner
entries.definitionCN: 决出胜者的一系列比赛

entries.definition: a group of teams that compete regularly
the official name of a sporting honour

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the -ship suffix and the link back to champion.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 -ship 后缀以及它与 champion 的联系。

normal.en: Championship is champion plus -ship, the state of being the best.
normal.cn: championship 就是 champion 加 -ship，即「最佳者」的身份。

normal.en: The suffix -ship also appears in friendship and leadership, all naming a state.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ship 也出现在 friendship 与 leadership 中，都表示一种状态。

normal.en: A championship is the contest, and the championship is also the title.
normal.cn: a championship 指那场比赛，the championship 也可指那个头衔。

normal.en: Win the championship, then defend the championship; the two phrases cover a career.
normal.cn: 先 win the championship，再 defend the championship，两个搭配概括了一段职业生涯。

normal.en: The plural championships simply adds an s to the long noun.
normal.cn: 复数 championships 只是在这个长名词后加 s。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy belt being fastened around a winner's waist.
abstract.cn: 想象一条厚重的腰带被系在胜者腰上。

abstract.en: Picture a scoreboard frozen at the final second of a long season.
abstract.cn: 想象漫长赛季最后一秒定格的记分牌。

abstract.en: Picture a cabinet crowded with cups from many years.
abstract.cn: 想象一个柜子塞满历年奖杯。

examples.en: The championship was decided in the last minute.
examples.cn: 冠军在最后一分钟才决出。

examples.en: Our school won the regional championship twice.
examples.cn: 我们学校两次赢得地区锦标赛。

examples.en: She defended her championship against a younger rival.
examples.cn: 她面对更年轻的对手成功卫冕。

dict_mnemonic.text: championship 是 champion 加 -ship：冠军加上表示身份的后缀，就是冠军头衔，也指争夺它的锦标赛。

root: 由 champion（源自拉丁语 campus 场地、campio 决斗者）加本土后缀 -ship（表示状态、职位）构成。

sensesIntro.en: The suffix first names the contest that produces a champion, then the rank that contest confers.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个后缀先指产出冠军的比赛，再指比赛授予的等级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a title held by the person left standing.
core.cn: 核心意象：由站到最后的人持有的头衔。

branches.en: A national championship is a long contest among teams.
branches.cn: 全国锦标赛是队伍之间的长期比赛。

branches.en: Holding the championship means holding the rank.
branches.cn: 持有冠军称号即持有这一等级。

branches.en: The final game decides the contest.
branches.cn: 决赛决定整项赛事的结果。

branches.en: The contest and the title share one name.
branches.cn: 比赛与头衔共用一个名称。

branches.en: Defending a championship is keeping the rank.
branches.cn: 卫冕就是保住这一等级。

intro.en: Championship joins a Latin field root to a native suffix of state.
intro.cn: championship 把拉丁语场地词根与本土状态后缀结合在一起。

latinIntro.en: The stem comes from Latin campus and campio; the suffix is native English -ship.
latinIntro.cn: 词干来自拉丁语 campus 与 campio，后缀则是英语本土的 -ship。

items.meaning: an informal word for a champion

items.example: Campio is the old fighter word.
Campus gave the stem its shape.
items.exampleCN: campus 给出了词干的形态。

latinEntries.exampleCN: campio 是 champion 背后的词。
campus 是比赛场地的名称。

definition_en: an opportunity to do something, the likelihood that something will happen, or the way events happen without plan
core_image: 骰子在桌面上翻滚，停在哪一面全凭偶然
scene: 云层压得很低，空气里带着湿气。There is a chance of rain before noon.
sceneCN: 这里 chance 指「可能性」（第 2 个义项：某事发生的可能程度）；句意是中午之前有下雨的可能。

senses.title: An opportunity to act
senses.definition: a situation that makes it possible for you to do something you want
senses.definitionCN: 使你有望做成想做之事的情形
senses.example: This is my last chance to qualify.
senses.exampleCN: 这是我获得资格的最后机会。
senses.why: A throw of the dice opened one outcome among many, and an opening for action took the same name.
senses.whyCN: 掷一次骰子会在众多结果中开出一面，行动的口子也就沿用了这个名字。

senses.title: The likelihood of an event
senses.definition: the degree to which something is likely to happen
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生的可能程度
senses.example: There is little chance of snow tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚下雪的可能性很小。
senses.why: The fall of the dice could be read as the odds of a result, not merely as luck.
senses.whyCN: 骰子的落点可以被读成某个结果的出现几率，而不只是运气。

senses.title: Luck or accident
senses.definition: the way events happen without being planned or controlled
senses.definitionCN: 事情未经计划与控制而发生的状态
senses.example: They met by chance at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在车站偶然相遇。
senses.why: When dice decide an outcome, people credit the result to accident rather than design.
senses.whyCN: 当骰子决定结果时，人们把结局归为偶然而非安排。

intro.en: Chance began as the Latin word for dice falling, and the falling became luck, likelihood and opportunity.
intro.cn: chance 起初是拉丁语中骰子落下的说法，这一「落下」后来变成运气、几率与机会。

items.en: Cadere meant to fall.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cadere 意为落下。

items.en: Cadentia named the falling of dice in a game.
items.cn: cadentia 指游戏中骰子的落下。

items.en: Cheance carried the sense of the way dice happened to fall.
items.cn: cheance 带有骰子碰巧落成怎样的意思。

items.en: English chance first meant a game result and then any unplanned event.
items.cn: 英语 chance 先指游戏结果，后指任何未加计划的事。

items.en: The word now covers luck, probability and a favourable opening.
items.cn: 如今该词涵盖运气、概率与有利的时机。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ch- onset, while the meaning group names openings and luck.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ch- 起首音，近义组列出时机与运气。

entries.definition: to become or make different
risky and uncertain
to sing words over and over
a favourable moment for action
good or bad fortune that comes by accident
entries.definitionCN: 偶然降临的好运或坏运

entries.definition: something that may happen

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the falling dice, the phrase by chance and the pattern chance of doing.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用落下的骰子、短语 by chance 以及 chance of doing 的句式。

normal.en: Chance and cadence share the Latin idea of falling, one for dice and one for rhythm.
normal.cn: chance 与 cadence 共享拉丁语「落下」之意，一个指骰子，一个指节拍。

normal.en: By chance is the shortest way to say that no one planned it.
normal.cn: by chance 是「没人安排」最简短的说法。

normal.en: Take a chance means you accept the dice may fall badly.
normal.cn: take a chance 意为接受骰子可能落得很糟。

normal.en: A chance of rain is a probability, not an invitation.
normal.cn: a chance of rain 说的是概率，不是邀请。

normal.en: The plural chances appears in phrases about odds, as in the chances are slim.
normal.cn: 复数 chances 出现在谈几率的说法里，如 the chances are slim。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of dice spinning across a wooden table.
abstract.cn: 想象一对骰子在木桌上旋转。

abstract.en: Picture a door opening for one second and then closing.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门只开了一秒又关上。

abstract.en: Picture two old friends meeting at a crowded station by accident.
abstract.cn: 想象两位老友在拥挤的车站不期而遇。

examples.en: Everyone deserves a fair chance to speak.
examples.cn: 每个人都应有公平发言的机会。

examples.en: The chances of finding the letter are small.
examples.cn: 找到那封信的可能性很小。

examples.en: I came across the shop by chance.
examples.cn: 我偶然发现了这家店。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 chance 想成「禅寺」的谐音：在禅寺门口与旧友偶遇，全凭机会与运气。

root: 源自拉丁语 cadere（落下）的派生形式 cadentia（骰子落下），经古法语 cheance 进入英语，词义由「骰子落点」扩展为运气、几率与机会。

sensesIntro.en: Dice that fall without plan give luck first, then the odds of a result, then the opening that result offers.
sensesIntro.cn: 无计划落下的骰子先给出运气，再给出结果的几率，最后给出该结果带来的时机。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: dice falling and settling on one face.
core.cn: 核心意象：骰子翻滚后停在某一面。

branches.en: A chance to speak is an opening offered by circumstance.
branches.cn: a chance to speak 是环境给出的开口。

branches.en: A chance of rain measures how likely the event is.
branches.cn: a chance of rain 衡量事件发生的可能。

branches.en: Meeting by chance means no one arranged it.
branches.cn: meeting by chance 意为无人安排。

branches.en: Luck and opportunity both depend on the roll.
branches.cn: 运气与机会都取决于那一掷。

branches.en: Probability and accident share the same image of falling.
branches.cn: 概率与偶然共享同一个「落下」意象。

intro.en: Chance keeps the -cad- falling root in chancy and mischance.
intro.cn: chance 在 chancy 与 mischance 中保留 -cad-「落下」词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin cadere and cadentia are the falling verb and noun behind the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cadere 与 cadentia 是英语这个词背后的「落下」动词与名词。

items.exampleCN: 那个计划看起来靠不住。

items.example: By mischance the letter arrived late.
Cadere is the old falling verb.
items.exampleCN: cadere 是古老的「落下」动词。

items.example: Cadentia named a throw of dice.
The occasion called for a speech.
items.exampleCN: 这个场合需要一篇讲话。

latinEntries.example: Cadere is the source of cadence.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cadere 是 cadence 的来源。
cadentia 在法语中变成 cheance。

definition_en: to become or make something different, a difference in a situation, coins and small notes, or a transfer to another vehicle
core_image: 旧样子被一面镜子换成了新样子
scene: 清晨的街道一夜之间换了模样。The city has changed a lot in ten years.
sceneCN: 这里 change 指「改变」（第 1 个义项：变得不同）；句意是这座城市在十年间变化很大。

senses.title: To become different
senses.definition: to become different, or to make something different
senses.definitionCN: 自身变得不同，或使某物变得不同
senses.example: The weather changed suddenly.
senses.exampleCN: 天气突然变了。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to exchange one thing for another, and exchanging an old state for a new one is change.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为以物易物，把旧状态换成新状态就是改变。

senses.title: Coins and small notes
senses.definition: money in the form of coins or notes of low value
senses.definitionCN: 以硬币或小面额纸币形式存在的钱
senses.example: Do you have change for a twenty-pound note?
senses.exampleCN: 你有一张二十镑的零钱吗？
senses.why: In old trade a large coin was exchanged for smaller ones, so the small money kept the name of the exchange.
senses.whyCN: 旧时交易把大额硬币换成小额，小额钱币便沿用了「兑换」之名。

senses.title: A transfer between vehicles
senses.definition: the act of leaving one bus, train or plane and boarding another
senses.definitionCN: 离开一辆车、一列火车或一架飞机并换乘另一辆的行为
senses.example: The journey needs one change in Paris.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟行程要在巴黎换乘一次。
senses.why: Travellers exchanged one carriage for another, so the switch itself was called a change.
senses.whyCN: 旅客把一节车厢换成另一节，这一转换本身就被称作 change。

intro.en: Change comes from a Latin verb of exchange, and the idea of swapping grew into becoming different.
intro.cn: change 源自拉丁语表示交换的动词，交换的观念逐渐生长为「变得不同」。

items.en: Cambire meant to exchange or barter.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cambire 意为交换或以物易物。

items.en: Cambiare widened the verb to cover any swapping.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 cambiare 把这个动词扩展到任何形式的互换。

items.en: Changier carried the verb into French with the sense of altering.
items.cn: changier 把该动词带入法语，带有「使不同」之意。

items.en: English change meant both to exchange and to become other.
items.cn: 英语 change 同时表示交换与变成另一状态。

items.en: The noun now also means small coins and a transfer between lines.
items.cn: 名词如今还指零钱与线路之间的换乘。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ch- shape, while the meaning group lists verbs of making different.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ch- 外形，近义组列出「使不同」的动词。

entries.definition: an opportunity or likelihood
to give one thing and receive another
entries.definitionCN: 给出一样并得到另一样

entries.definition: never altering
to make something different in part
to differ or make different
to change something slightly

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the exchange root, the coin sense and the fixed phrases with change.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「交换」词根、零钱义以及含 change 的固定搭配。

normal.en: Change and exchange both come from a Latin verb of swapping.
normal.cn: change 与 exchange 都来自拉丁语表示互换的动词。

normal.en: Change your mind is a swap of one opinion for another.
normal.cn: change your mind 就是用一个想法换掉另一个。

normal.en: Small change is what you get after a large note is exchanged.
normal.cn: small change 就是大钞被换开后到手的小钱。

normal.en: Change trains repeats the word because you swap one train for another.
normal.cn: change trains 重复这个词，因为你是用一列火车换另一列。

normal.en: The plural changes and the participle changing both keep the soft g sound.
normal.cn: 复数 changes 与分词 changing 都保留软 g 的读音。

abstract.en: Picture a grey street turning bright after rain.
abstract.cn: 想象灰色的街道在雨后变得明亮。

abstract.en: Picture a handful of coins dropped on a counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一把硬币落在柜台上。

abstract.en: Picture a traveller stepping off one train and onto another.
abstract.cn: 想象旅客从一列火车跨上另一列。

examples.en: The rules may change next year.
examples.cn: 规则明年可能会变。

examples.en: Keep the change, please.
examples.cn: 零钱请留着吧。

examples.en: We changed planes in Hong Kong.
examples.cn: 我们在香港换了飞机。

dict_mnemonic.text: change 与 exchange 同一源：exchange 是交换，change 就是把旧的换成新的，也就是改变。

root: 源自拉丁语 cambire（交换），经晚期拉丁语 cambiare 与古法语 changier 进入英语，词义由「互换」扩展为改变、零钱与换乘。

sensesIntro.en: Swapping one thing for another first gives alteration, then small coins, then a switch of vehicles.
sensesIntro.cn: 以物换物先给出改变，再给出零钱，最后给出交通工具的转换。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one thing exchanged for another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一样东西被换成另一样。

branches.en: To change is to swap an old state for a new one.
branches.cn: 改变就是把旧状态换成新状态。

branches.en: Small change is money produced by a swap.
branches.cn: 零钱是兑换产生的小额钱币。

branches.en: A change of trains swaps one carriage for another.
branches.cn: 换乘就是把一列车换成另一列。

branches.en: Both senses keep the old sense of exchange.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留古老的交换含义。

branches.en: Alteration and transfer are both moves to another state.
branches.cn: 改变与换乘都是转向另一状态。

intro.en: Change keeps the -chang- stem in changeable, unchanged and exchange.
intro.cn: change 在 changeable、unchanged 与 exchange 中保留 -chang- 词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin cambire and cambiare are the exchange verbs that produced French changier.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cambire 与 cambiare 是产出法语 changier 的「交换」动词。

items.meaning: in the process of becoming different

definition_en: a television or radio station, a passage through which water or information moves, or a narrow stretch of sea
core_image: 一条被水流长期冲出的窄沟
scene: 山谷深处的岩壁被水磨得光滑。The river cut a narrow channel through the rock.
sceneCN: 这里 channel 指「水道；通道」（第 2 个义项：水或其他事物通过的路径）；句意是河水在岩石间冲出一条狭窄的水道。

senses.title: A television or radio band
senses.definition: a band of frequencies used by a particular television or radio station
senses.definitionCN: 某家电视台或电台使用的频段
senses.example: Switch to another channel after the news.
senses.exampleCN: 新闻结束后换到另一个频道。
senses.why: Broadcasting needed a word for a path that carries a signal, and the waterway word supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 广播需要一个表示信号通路的词，而水道这个词正好补上。

senses.title: A passage for water or information
senses.definition: a passage through which water, goods or information moves
senses.definitionCN: 水、货物或信息通过的路径
senses.example: The river cut a narrow channel through the rock.
senses.exampleCN: 河水在岩石间冲出一条狭窄的水道。
senses.why: The Latin base meant a pipe or groove, the exact shape of any narrow passage.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词基意为管道或沟槽，正是任何狭窄通道的形状。

senses.title: A narrow sea passage
senses.definition: a narrow stretch of water between two areas of land
senses.definitionCN: 两片陆地之间的狭长水域
senses.example: Ships waited for calm weather to cross the channel.
senses.exampleCN: 船只等待风平浪静时穿越海峡。
senses.why: A groove filled with sea water is simply the waterway sense on a map-sized scale.
senses.whyCN: 灌满海水的沟槽，不过是水道义在地图尺度上的放大。

intro.en: Channel goes back to a Latin word for a pipe, and every later sense keeps that shape of a narrow passage.
intro.cn: channel 可追溯到拉丁语表示管道的词，后来各义项都保留狭窄通路这一形状。

items.en: Canalis meant a pipe, groove or water channel.
items.cn: 拉丁语 canalis 意为管道、沟槽或水道。

items.en: Chanel named a bed of a stream or a narrow sea passage.
items.cn: chanel 指河床或狭窄的海上通道。

items.en: English channel first described a watercourse and a strait.
items.cn: 英语 channel 先描述水道与海峡。

items.en: The word extended to any route by which something travels.
items.cn: 该词扩展到任何事物通行的路线。

items.en: Radio and television gave it the sense of a broadcast band.
items.cn: 广播与电视赋予它播出频段的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the canal shape, while the meaning group lists other passages and routes.
note.cn: 形近组共享 canal 的外形，近义组列出其他通道与路线。

entries.definition: a man-made waterway
the area around the altar of a church
more than one channel
a way through something
a way from one place to another
entries.definitionCN: 从一处到另一处的路线

entries.definition: a narrow passage of water

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the canal root, the sea strait and the phrase through official channels.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 canal 词根、海峡义以及短语 through official channels。

normal.en: Channel and canal are twins from the Latin word for a pipe.
normal.cn: channel 与 canal 是拉丁语「管道」一词的双胞胎。

normal.en: A television channel is a groove cut for a signal instead of water.
normal.cn: 电视频道就是为信号而非水流开出的沟。

normal.en: Through official channels means by the proper route, not by a shortcut.
normal.cn: through official channels 意为走正规路线，而非抄近路。

normal.en: The English Channel is simply the waterway sense written on a map.
normal.cn: the English Channel 不过是水道义写在地图上。

normal.en: The verb channel takes resources as its object, as in channel funds into schools.
normal.cn: 动词 channel 以资源为宾语，如 channel funds into schools。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow groove in stone with water running through it.
abstract.cn: 想象石头上一条窄沟，水从中流过。

abstract.en: Picture a remote control clicking from one station to the next.
abstract.cn: 想象遥控器从一个台跳到下一个台。

abstract.en: Picture ships queuing between two headlands in grey weather.
abstract.cn: 想象灰暗天气里船只在两处海角间排队。

examples.en: The interview will be shown on channel four.
examples.cn: 这次采访将在第四频道播出。

examples.en: Complaints should go through the proper channels.
examples.cn: 投诉应通过正当渠道提出。

examples.en: They channelled the extra money into research.
examples.cn: 他们把额外的钱投入研究。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 channel 想成 canal（运河）：运河是水的频道，电视频道是信号的运河。

root: 源自拉丁语 canalis（管道、沟槽），经古法语 chanel 进入英语；与 canal 同源，核心形状是狭长的通路。

sensesIntro.en: A groove for water becomes a passage for goods and news, a strait on the map and a band for broadcast.
sensesIntro.cn: 流水的沟槽变成货物与消息的通道，再变成地图上的海峡与播出的频段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow groove that carries something along.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条把某物往前输送的窄沟。

branches.en: A broadcast band is a channel for a signal.
branches.cn: 播出频段是信号的通道。

branches.en: A river channel is the oldest and most physical sense.
branches.cn: 河道是最古老也最具体的义项。

branches.en: A strait is a channel at the scale of a map.
branches.cn: 海峡是地图尺度上的通道。

branches.en: Both keep the image of water finding a narrow way.
branches.cn: 两者都保留水寻找窄路的意象。

branches.en: Information now flows where water once flowed.
branches.cn: 如今信息在昔日水流之处流动。

intro.en: Channel keeps the -canal- root in canal, channelization and multichannel.
intro.cn: channel 在 canal、channelization 与 multichannel 中保留 -canal- 词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin canalis is the pipe that gave both channel and canal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 canalis 就是给出 channel 与 canal 的那根管道。

items.example: The channel was full of mud.
They channelled water to the field.
She is channelling her energy into work.
Canalis is the old pipe word.
The tunnel runs under the river.

latinEntries.exampleCN: canalis 在法语中变成 chanel。

latinEntries.example: Canal is the twin of channel.
latinEntries.exampleCN: canal 是 channel 的双胞胎。

definition_en: a state of complete disorder, or the formless void believed to exist before the ordered world
core_image: 所有东西同时散落，找不到任何次序
scene: 停电后路口乱成一团。Traffic fell into chaos after the lights failed.
sceneCN: 这里 chaos 指「混乱」（第 1 个义项：完全失去秩序的状态）；句意是信号灯失灵后交通陷入混乱。

senses.title: Complete disorder
senses.definition: a state in which everything is confused and has no order
senses.definitionCN: 一切事物都杂乱无章、毫无秩序的状态
senses.example: The office was in chaos after the move.
senses.exampleCN: 搬完之后办公室一片混乱。
senses.why: The Greek word named the void before creation, and any total loss of order recalls that void.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语原词指创世之前的虚空，任何彻底失序都让人想起那片虚空。

senses.title: The formless state before the world
senses.definition: the empty, formless state that Greek myth placed before the ordered universe
senses.definitionCN: 希腊神话置于有序宇宙之前的空虚无形状态
senses.example: Greek myths begin with chaos.
senses.exampleCN: 希腊神话从混沌开始。
senses.why: Hesiod used the word for the gap that opened before earth and sky were separated.
senses.whyCN: 赫西俄德用这个词指大地与天空分开之前张开的空隙。

senses.title: A jumble of unconnected things
senses.definition: a confused mass of objects or ideas with no pattern
senses.definitionCN: 毫无规律地堆在一起的物件或想法
senses.example: The desk was a chaos of papers and cups.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上是一堆杂乱的文件和杯子。
senses.why: A desk that loses every pattern is a small private copy of the original void.
senses.whyCN: 一张失去全部规律的桌子，就是那片原始虚空的小型私人翻版。

intro.en: Chaos is a Greek word for a gap or void, taken into English to name any total disorder.
intro.cn: chaos 是希腊语中表示裂缝或虚空的词，进入英语后指任何彻底的混乱。

items.en: Khaos meant a gap, chasm or empty space.
items.cn: 希腊语 khaos 意为裂缝、深渊或空旷之处。

items.en: Hesiod made Khaos the formless state before the gods.
items.cn: 赫西俄德把 khaos 写成众神之前的无形状态。

items.en: Latin chaos kept the cosmological sense of the void.
items.cn: 拉丁语 chaos 保留了虚空的宇宙论含义。

items.en: English chaos first described the state before creation.
items.cn: 英语 chaos 先描述创世之前的状态。

items.en: The word now also means any messy, uncontrolled situation.
items.cn: 如今该词也指任何杂乱失控的局面。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Greek stem, while the meaning group lists states of disorder.
note.cn: 形近组共享希腊语词干，近义组列出各种失序状态。

entries.definition: completely without order
a deep opening in the ground
the study of systems that look random
entries.definitionCN: 研究看似随机系统的学问

entries.definition: a lack of order
a state in which things are unclear
a dirty or untidy state

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Greek void, the chaotic adjective and the phrase in chaos.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用希腊语虚空、形容词 chaotic 以及短语 in chaos。

normal.en: Chaos is the gap before the world, so a chaotic room has lost its order.
normal.cn: chaos 是世界之前的裂缝，所以 chaotic 的房间就是失去了次序。

normal.en: The adjective chaotic adds -ic, and the adverb adds -ally.
normal.cn: 形容词 chaotic 加 -ic，副词再在其后加 -ally。

normal.en: In chaos needs no article, because the noun is uncountable.
normal.cn: in chaos 不加冠词，因为这个词不可数。

normal.en: Chaos theory studies systems whose starting point decides everything.
normal.cn: chaos theory 研究起点决定一切的系统。

normal.en: A chaos of papers describes a heap with no pattern at all.
normal.cn: a chaos of papers 描述完全没有规律的一堆纸。

abstract.en: Picture a room where every drawer has been emptied at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间，所有抽屉同时被倒空。

abstract.en: Picture a dark gap opening before the first light.
abstract.cn: 想象第一道光之前张开的黑暗裂缝。

abstract.en: Picture a crossroads with dead lights and honking cars.
abstract.cn: 想象一个信号灯全灭、汽车鸣笛的路口。

examples.en: The airport was in chaos after the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨过后机场一片混乱。

examples.en: He tried to bring order to the chaos of his notes.
examples.cn: 他试着把杂乱的笔记理出头绪。

examples.en: The old story says the world rose out of chaos.
examples.cn: 古老的故事说世界从混沌中升起。

dict_mnemonic.text: chaos 读起来像「吵死」：一群人吵得不可开交，场面就是一片混乱。

root: 源自希腊语 khaos（裂缝、虚空），经拉丁语 chaos 进入英语，由「创世前的无形虚空」引申为彻底的混乱。

sensesIntro.en: The empty gap before creation gives the mythic sense first, then any total disorder, then a mere jumble.
sensesIntro.cn: 创世前的空虚先给出神话义，再给出彻底的混乱，最后给出普通的一堆杂物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a formless gap where nothing has its place.
core.cn: 核心意象：万物都找不到位置的无形空隙。

branches.en: A chaotic office has lost every pattern.
branches.cn: 混乱的办公室失去了全部规律。

branches.en: Myth places chaos before earth and sky.
branches.cn: 神话把混沌放在天地之前。

branches.en: A heap of papers is chaos on a small scale.
branches.cn: 一堆纸是缩小尺度的混乱。

branches.en: Both senses share the idea of no order at all.
branches.cn: 两个义项都共享「全无秩序」的意思。

branches.en: The everyday mess echoes the cosmic void.
branches.cn: 日常的杂乱呼应着宇宙的虚空。

intro.en: Chaos forms chaotic and chaotically with the adjective and adverb endings.
intro.cn: chaos 借助形容词与副词词尾构成 chaotic 与 chaotically。

latinIntro.en: The word passed from Greek khaos into Latin chaos before reaching English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词从希腊语 khaos 进入拉丁语 chaos，再到英语。

items.meaning: a deep gap in the earth
items.example: A chasm opened in the road.

latinEntries.example: Latin chaos kept the Greek sense.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 chaos 保留了希腊语义。

definition_en: a man or boy, used in a friendly informal way, or a painful crack in the skin
core_image: 一个穿着旧外套、笑着打招呼的年轻男子
scene: 门口站着一个瘦高的年轻人。A tall chap in a grey coat asked for directions.
sceneCN: 这里 chap 指「小伙子；家伙」（第 1 个义项：对男子的非正式称呼）；句意是门口一个穿灰大衣的高个年轻人来问路。

senses.title: A man or boy
senses.definition: a man or boy, used in an informal and friendly way
senses.definitionCN: 对男子或男孩的非正式、友善的称呼
senses.example: He is a decent chap.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个正派的小伙子。
senses.why: The word began as a shortening of chapman, a trader, and then slid from merchant to any fellow.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初是 chapman（商人）的缩略，随后从商人滑向任何男子。

senses.title: A crack in the skin
senses.definition: a painful split in the skin, especially on the hands or lips
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤上疼痛的裂口，尤见于手部或嘴唇
senses.example: The cold wind left chaps on his hands.
senses.exampleCN: 冷风在他手上留下了裂口。
senses.why: A separate old verb meaning to split open gave this sense, which happens to share the spelling.
senses.whyCN: 另一个意为裂开的古动词给出了这个义项，恰好共用同一拼写。

senses.title: To crack from cold
senses.definition: to become rough and split because of cold or dry air
senses.definitionCN: 因寒冷或干燥而变得粗糙开裂
senses.example: My lips chap in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 我的嘴唇冬天会皲裂。
senses.why: The splitting verb stayed in use for skin, so the noun and the verb keep one shape.
senses.whyCN: 表示裂开的动词一直用于皮肤，于是名词与动词保持同一形态。

intro.en: Chap has two histories: a shortening of chapman the trader, and an old verb meaning to split.
intro.cn: chap 有两段历史：一是商人 chapman 的缩略，二是意为裂开的古动词。

items.en: Ceapman meant a merchant or trader.
items.cn: 古英语 ceapman 意为商人或买卖人。

items.en: Chap shortened chapman and came to mean any man.
items.cn: chap 缩短了 chapman，转而指任何男子。

items.en: A separate verb chappen meant to crack open.
items.cn: 另一个动词 chappen 意为裂开。

items.en: Chapped skin kept the crack sense in daily use.
items.cn: 皲裂的皮肤让「裂开」义留在了日常用法里。

items.en: The friendly fellow sense and the skin sense now live side by side.
items.cn: 友善的男子义与皮肤裂口义如今并存。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the trader root, while the meaning group lists words for a man.
note.cn: 形近组共享商人词根，近义组列出指男子的词。

entries.definition: an old word for a travelling seller
costing little money
rough and split by cold
a man, used informally
an informal word for a man
a British word for a man
entries.definitionCN: 英式英语中指男子的词

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the trader root, the friendly phrase old chap and the skin sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用商人词根、友好说法 old chap 以及皮肤义。

normal.en: Chap was once chapman, the trader who walked from town to town.
normal.cn: chap 原本是 chapman，即走村串镇的商人。

normal.en: Old chap is the phrase that shows the word is warm rather than formal.
normal.cn: old chap 这个说法表明该词温暖而非正式。

normal.en: Chapped lips repeat the crack sense in a phrase you can see.
normal.cn: chapped lips 把「裂开」义放进一个看得见的搭配里。

normal.en: The plural chaps is both several men and several cracks.
normal.cn: 复数 chaps 既指几个男子，也指几道裂口。

normal.en: Remember cheap shares the trader root, since bargaining and selling belong together.
normal.cn: 记住 cheap 共享商人词根，因为讨价与买卖本是一体。

abstract.en: Picture a friendly stranger tipping his hat at a door.
abstract.cn: 想象一个友善的陌生人在门口抬帽致意。

abstract.en: Picture red cracked knuckles after a day in the wind.
abstract.cn: 想象吹了一天风后发红开裂的指节。

abstract.en: Picture a pedlar with a heavy pack on a country road.
abstract.cn: 想象乡间小路上背着沉重货包的小贩。

examples.en: The chap at the desk helped me at once.
examples.cn: 柜台后的那个小伙子马上帮了我。

examples.en: He is a funny old chap.
examples.cn: 他是个有趣的老家伙。

examples.en: Her hands chapped badly in the dry air.
examples.cn: 干燥的空气让她的手严重皲裂。

dict_mnemonic.text: chap 与 cheap 同源：小贩 chapman 讨价还价，后来 chap 就指街上随便一个家伙。

root: 表示「男子」的 chap 是 chapman（古英语 ceapman，商人）的缩略，与 cheap 同源；表示「皲裂」的 chap 来自中古英语 chappen（裂开），两词同形异源。

sensesIntro.en: A trader shortened into any fellow gives the friendly sense, while a splitting verb gives the skin sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 商人一词缩略为任何男子，给出友善义；裂开的动词则给出皮肤义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cheerful fellow met by chance on the road.
core.cn: 核心意象：在路上偶遇的一个快活家伙。

branches.en: A decent chap is a friendly judgement about a man.
branches.cn: a decent chap 是对一个男子的友善评价。

branches.en: A chap on the hand is a painful split.
branches.cn: 手上的 chap 是一道疼痛的裂口。

branches.en: The verb describes lips splitting in cold air.
branches.cn: 动词描述嘴唇在冷空气中裂开。

branches.en: One spelling carries two unrelated histories.
branches.cn: 一个拼写承载两段不相干的历史。

branches.en: The noun and verb of cracking share one shape.
branches.cn: 裂开的名词与动词共用一个形态。

intro.en: Chap keeps the trader root in chapman and the splitting root in chapped.
intro.cn: chap 在 chapman 中保留商人词根，在 chapped 中保留裂开词根。

latinIntro.en: The trader sense goes back to Old English ceap, a bargain, the same root as cheap.
latinIntro.cn: 商人义可追溯到古英语 ceap（交易），与 cheap 同根。

items.example: Ceap is the old trade word.

items.meaning: an informal word for a man

definition_en: a main division of a book, a distinct period in a history or life, or a local branch of an organization
core_image: 一本书被书签分开的一段
scene: 夜深了，书页翻到新的部分。She stopped reading at the third chapter.
sceneCN: 这里 chapter 指「章」（第 1 个义项：书中的主要分节）；句意是她在第三章停下阅读。

senses.title: A main division of a book
senses.definition: one of the main parts into which a book or long text is divided
senses.definitionCN: 书或长文被分成的主要部分之一
senses.example: The first chapter sets the scene.
senses.exampleCN: 第一章交代了背景。
senses.why: Latin capitulum meant a little head, the heading written at the start of each section.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 capitulum 意为小头，即写在每节开头的小标题。

senses.title: A period in a life or history
senses.definition: a distinct period in someone's life or in the history of something
senses.definitionCN: 某人一生或某事历史中界限分明的一段
senses.example: That chapter of her life is closed.
senses.exampleCN: 她人生的那一章已经翻过去了。
senses.why: A section of a story was borrowed for a stretch of time that reads like a story.
senses.whyCN: 故事的一节被借来形容一段读起来像故事的时间。

senses.title: A local branch of a society
senses.definition: a local branch of a club, society or religious body
senses.definitionCN: 俱乐部、协会或宗教团体的地方分支
senses.example: The local chapter meets on Fridays.
senses.exampleCN: 地方分会每周五聚会。
senses.why: Members gathered under one heading formed a chapter, and the word passed to the group itself.
senses.whyCN: 在同一标题下聚集的成员构成一个 chapter，这个词又转指这群人本身。

intro.en: Chapter descends from Latin caput, a head, through the little heading written at the start of a section.
intro.cn: chapter 源自拉丁语 caput（头），经由写在一节开头的小标题而来。

items.en: Caput meant the head.
items.cn: 拉丁语 caput 意为头。

items.en: Capitulum was a little head, used for a heading.
items.cn: capitulum 意为小头，用来指标题。

items.en: Chapitre named a division of a book and a body of clergy.
items.cn: chapitre 指书中的分节，也指一群教士。

items.en: English chapter named both a book section and a cathedral body.
items.cn: 英语 chapter 同时指书中分节与主教座堂的教士团。

items.en: The word now also means a period of time and a local branch.
items.cn: 如今该词还指一段时期与地方分会。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cap- head root, while the meaning group lists parts and phases.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cap-「头」词根，近义组列出部分与阶段。

entries.definition: the chief city or money for investment
the leader of a team or ship
more than one chapter
one part of a whole text
one event in a longer series
entries.definitionCN: 较长系列中的一个事件

entries.definition: a local office of an organization

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the head root, the phrase a new chapter and the local branch sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「头」词根、短语 a new chapter 以及地方分会义。

normal.en: Chapter and capital share caput, the Latin head, because a chapter begins with a heading.
normal.cn: chapter 与 capital 共享拉丁语 caput（头），因为一章从一个标题开始。

normal.en: A new chapter is a fresh period, not a new book.
normal.cn: a new chapter 指新的阶段，而不是一本新书。

normal.en: Chapter and verse means you can cite the exact place.
normal.cn: chapter and verse 意为能引出确切出处。

normal.en: A local chapter is a branch that meets under one name.
normal.cn: local chapter 是在同一名下聚会的地方分支。

normal.en: The plural chapters adds an s and appears in chapter titles.
normal.cn: 复数 chapters 加 s，常出现在章节标题里。

abstract.en: Picture a bookmark closing one part of a story.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚书签合上故事的一段。

abstract.en: Picture a turned page with a large number at the top.
abstract.cn: 想象翻过的一页，顶端印着大大的数字。

abstract.en: Picture a small group of members raising hands in a side room.
abstract.cn: 想象一小群成员在小房间里举手。

examples.en: The book has twelve chapters.
examples.cn: 这本书有十二章。

examples.en: Moving abroad opened a new chapter in his life.
examples.cn: 移居国外为他的人生打开了新篇章。

examples.en: The student chapter organized a charity run.
examples.cn: 学生分会组织了一场慈善长跑。

dict_mnemonic.text: chapter 与 capital 同源，都来自「头」（caput）：一章就是一段文字的「头」。

root: 源自拉丁语 caput（头）的指小形式 capitulum（小头、标题），经古法语 chapitre 进入英语；与 capital、captain 同根。

sensesIntro.en: A heading marks off a book section, and that section became a period of time and a branch of members.
sensesIntro.cn: 标题划出书中的一节，这一节又变成一段时期与一群成员的分支。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heading that opens a new section.
core.cn: 核心意象：开启新一节的那个标题。

branches.en: A chapter heading divides a long text.
branches.cn: 章节标题把长文分开。

branches.en: A closed chapter marks the end of a period.
branches.cn: 翻过去的一章标志一段时期的结束。

branches.en: A local chapter gathers members under one heading.
branches.cn: 地方分会在同一标题下聚集成员。

branches.en: Both senses borrow the shape of a story.
branches.cn: 两个义项都借用了故事的形态。

branches.en: Text divisions and member groups share the heading.
branches.cn: 文本分节与成员团体共享「标题」。

intro.en: Chapter keeps the cap- head root found in capital and captain.
intro.cn: chapter 保留在 capital 与 captain 中可见的 cap-「头」词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin caput and its diminutive capitulum are the head and the heading behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 caput 及其指小形式 capitulum 是这个词背后的「头」与「标题」。

items.meaning: a meeting house of a branch

items.example: The capital lies to the north.

definition_en: the qualities that make a person or place distinct, a person in a story, or a letter or symbol used in writing
core_image: 刻在金属上的一枚印记，显示物件的本色
scene: 小说里的老人沉默而固执。The old man in the novel is a memorable character.
sceneCN: 这里 character 指「人物」（第 2 个义项：故事中的人物）；句意是小说里的这位老人是个令人难忘的人物。

senses.title: The qualities of a person
senses.definition: the set of qualities that make a person or place what it is
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某地成为其自身的全部品质
senses.example: She has a strong character.
senses.exampleCN: 她性格坚强。
senses.why: Greek kharakter was the mark stamped on a coin, an outward sign of what lay inside.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 kharakter 是压在硬币上的印记，是内在之物的外在标志。

senses.title: A person in a story
senses.definition: a person in a novel, play or film
senses.definitionCN: 小说、戏剧或电影中的人物
senses.example: The old man in the novel is a memorable character.
senses.exampleCN: 小说里的这位老人是个令人难忘的人物。
senses.why: Writers borrowed the stamped mark for the figures stamped into a story.
senses.whyCN: 作家把压印的记号借来，指被压进故事里的那些人物。

senses.title: A letter or symbol
senses.definition: a letter, number or symbol used in writing or printing
senses.definitionCN: 书写或印刷所用的字母、数字或符号
senses.example: The password needs eight characters.
senses.exampleCN: 密码需要八个字符。
senses.why: A stamped mark is literally a written sign, so the alphabet sense is the oldest of all.
senses.whyCN: 压出的印记本就是一种书写符号，所以字符义其实最为古老。

intro.en: Character began as a Greek word for an engraved mark and grew into nature, symbol and story figure.
intro.cn: character 起初是希腊语中「刻痕」的说法，后来生长出本性、符号与故事人物诸义。

items.en: Kharakter meant an engraved mark or stamp.
items.cn: 希腊语 kharakter 意为刻出的痕迹或印章。

items.en: The word also named the distinctive stamp of a person's nature.
items.cn: 该词也指一个人本性上独有的印记。

items.en: Latin character kept both the written sign and the moral sense.
items.cn: 拉丁语 character 同时保留书写符号与品格两义。

items.en: English character first meant a written symbol.
items.cn: 英语 character 最初指书写符号。

items.en: The word now covers personality, reputation and people in fiction.
items.cn: 如今该词涵盖性格、名声与虚构作品中的人物。

note.en: The look-alike group builds on the same stem, while the meaning group lists nature and symbol words.
note.cn: 形近组由同一词干构成，近义组列出本性词与符号词。

entries.definition: a typical feature
to describe the nature of something
more than one character
the pattern of a person's behaviour
entries.definitionCN: 一个人行为的整体模式

entries.definition: a person shown in a story or picture
entries.definitionCN: 故事或图画中出现的人物

entries.definition: a sign that stands for something

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the engraved mark, the Chinese character phrase and the story sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用刻痕意象、短语 Chinese character 以及故事人物义。

normal.en: Character and carve share the idea of cutting a mark into a surface.
normal.cn: character 与 carve 共享在表面刻下痕迹的意思。

normal.en: A Chinese character is literally a written mark, the oldest sense of the word.
normal.cn: a Chinese character 本就是一个书写记号，正是这个词最古老的义项。

normal.en: In character means the action fits the mark already stamped on the person.
normal.cn: in character 意为行为符合早已印在那人身上的记号。

normal.en: A main character carries the plot, just as a stamp carries a claim.
normal.cn: main character 承载情节，正如印章承载声明。

normal.en: The plural characters covers letters, people and personal traits at once.
normal.cn: 复数 characters 同时涵盖字符、人物与性格特征。

abstract.en: Picture a hot stamp pressed into soft wax.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚滚烫的印章压进软蜡。

abstract.en: Picture a novel where one old man keeps returning.
abstract.cn: 想象一部小说里有一位反复出现的老者。

abstract.en: Picture a password box asking for eight signs.
abstract.cn: 想象一个密码框要求输入八个符号。

examples.en: The town has a character of its own.
examples.cn: 这座小镇自有其特色。

examples.en: The two characters meet again at the end.
examples.cn: 两个人物在结尾重逢。

examples.en: Write your name in capital characters.
examples.cn: 请用大写字母写你的名字。

dict_mnemonic.text: character 与「刻」有关：希腊语原义是刻下的印记，性格就是刻在人身上的记号。

root: 源自希腊语 kharakter（刻痕、印记），经拉丁语 character 进入英语；核心是「刻下的记号」，由此引申出符号、性格与人物。

sensesIntro.en: A stamp makes a written sign, marks a person's nature and presses a figure into a story.
sensesIntro.cn: 一枚印章既留下书写符号，也标记人的本性，还把人物压进故事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mark cut into a surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：刻进表面的一个记号。

branches.en: A strong character is the mark of a settled nature.
branches.cn: 坚强的性格是稳定本性的记号。

branches.en: A story character is a figure stamped into fiction.
branches.cn: 故事人物是被压进虚构作品的形象。

branches.en: A character on a screen is the oldest literal sense.
branches.cn: 屏幕上的字符是最古老的字面义。

branches.en: Both senses rest on the idea of a distinguishing mark.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在「识别记号」之上。

branches.en: A person's nature and a story figure share one word.
branches.cn: 人的本性与故事人物共用一个词。

intro.en: Character keeps the -character- stem in characteristic, characterize and characterless.
intro.cn: character 在 characteristic、characterize 与 characterless 中保留 -character- 词干。

latinIntro.en: Greek kharakter passed through Latin character into English with the mark intact.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 kharakter 经拉丁语 character 进入英语，刻痕意象完好保留。

items.example: Critics characterize the style as spare.
items.exampleCN: 评论家把这种风格描述为简省。

items.meaning: the way a figure is drawn

latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 character 保留了这一记号。

definition_en: a quality that is typical of a person or thing, or being typical of a particular group
core_image: 一个人身上反复出现、可以辨认的记号
scene: 这种鸟的尾羽比身体长得多。A long tail is characteristic of the male bird.
sceneCN: 这里 characteristic 指「特有的；典型的」（第 2 个义项：某类事物明显具有的）；句意是长尾是这种雄鸟的典型特征。

senses.title: A typical feature
senses.definition: a quality that is typical of a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某物典型的品质
senses.example: Patience is her best characteristic.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心是她最突出的特点。
senses.why: The Greek adjective meant able to mark, so a characteristic is what marks a thing out.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语形容词意为能留下记号，因此特征是使某物得以辨识的记号。

senses.title: Typical of a group
senses.definition: being a typical quality of a particular person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 属于某人或某物典型性质的
senses.example: A long tail is characteristic of the male bird.
senses.exampleCN: 长尾是这种雄鸟的典型特征。
senses.why: The same adjective says that a mark belongs to a whole kind, not just one member.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形容词说明这个记号属于整个类别，而不只是某一个成员。

intro.en: Characteristic is the Greek adjective of marking, built on the same stem as character.
intro.cn: characteristic 是希腊语中表示「留下记号」的形容词，与 character 同词干。

items.en: Kharakter meant an engraved mark.
items.cn: 希腊语 kharakter 意为刻出的记号。

items.en: Kharakteristikos meant skilled at marking or distinctive.
items.cn: kharakteristikos 意为善于留下记号或有辨识度的。

items.en: Latin character and its adjective passed into scholarly use.
items.cn: 拉丁语 character 及其形容词进入学术用语。

items.en: English characteristic named a distinguishing quality.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语 characteristic 指有区分作用的品质。

items.en: The word now works as both a noun and an adjective.
items.cn: 如今该词既作名词也作形容词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the character stem, while the meaning group lists feature words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 character 词干，近义组列出表示特征的词。

entries.definition: the nature of a person
to describe the nature of something
in a way that is typical
a noticeable part of something
a particular quality of a person
showing the usual qualities of a group

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the mark root, the phrase be characteristic of and the noun ending -istic.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用记号词根、短语 be characteristic of 以及名词化词尾 -istic。

normal.en: Characteristic is the adjective of character, so it describes the mark a thing leaves.
normal.cn: characteristic 是 character 的形容词，因此描述事物留下的记号。

normal.en: Be characteristic of means the quality belongs to the whole kind.
normal.cn: be characteristic of 意为这种品质属于整个类别。

normal.en: A defining characteristic is the mark that decides identity.
normal.cn: a defining characteristic 是决定身份的那道记号。

normal.en: The adverb characteristically adds -ally to the same stem.
normal.cn: 副词 characteristically 是在同一词干后加 -ally。

normal.en: The plural characteristics names several marks at once.
normal.cn: 复数 characteristics 一次指出好几道记号。

abstract.en: Picture a bird with a tail far longer than its body.
abstract.cn: 想象一只尾巴远长于身体的鸟。

abstract.en: Picture a fingerprint that identifies one person only.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚只认出一个人的指纹。

abstract.en: Picture a list of family traits passed down the years.
abstract.cn: 想象一份代代相传的家族特征清单。

examples.en: The two species share several characteristics.
examples.cn: 这两个物种共有若干特征。

examples.en: Patience is characteristic of a good teacher.
examples.cn: 耐心是好老师的典型特征。

examples.en: Her style is characteristic of the period.
examples.cn: 她的风格是那个时期的典型风格。

dict_mnemonic.text: characteristic 是 character 加 -istic：一个人身上反复出现的记号，就是他的特征。

root: 源自希腊语 kharakteristikos（能留下记号的），与 character（刻痕）同词干，经拉丁语进入英语，指有辨识作用的品质。

sensesIntro.en: A mark that identifies a thing gives the noun a feature, and the same mark makes the adjective mean typical.
sensesIntro.cn: 辨识事物的记号给出名词「特征」，同一记号使形容词表示「典型的」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mark that tells one kind from another.
core.cn: 核心意象：把一类事物与另一类区分开的记号。

branches.en: Patience as a characteristic is a repeated mark.
branches.cn: 作为特征的耐心是一道反复出现的记号。

branches.en: A long tail marks the whole male group.
branches.cn: 长尾标记出整个雄性群体。

branches.en: Physical characteristics are marks you can observe.
branches.cn: 身体特征是可以观察到的记号。

branches.en: The noun names the mark, the adjective says it fits the kind.
branches.cn: 名词指那道记号，形容词说它契合该类。

branches.en: Be characteristic of links one mark to a whole class.
branches.cn: be characteristic of 把一道记号连到整个类别。

intro.en: Characteristic adds -istic to the character stem, and the adverb adds -ally.
intro.cn: characteristic 在 character 词干后加 -istic，副词再加 -ally。

latinIntro.en: Greek kharakter and kharakteristikos are the mark and the marking adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 kharakter 与 kharakteristikos 分别是记号与「留下记号」的形容词。

items.example: The characteristic is easy to see.
items.exampleCN: 这个特征很容易看出来。
寒冷的冬天是该地区的特点。

items.example: The nose is a useful feature.
items.exampleCN: 鼻子是有用的辨识部位。

latinEntries.example: Kharakter is the root of the family.

latinEntries.meaningCN: 能留下记号或作区分的

definition_en: to describe the typical qualities of a person or thing, or to be a typical quality of something
core_image: 用几笔勾出一个人最显眼的轮廓
scene: 评论家用一个词概括这座城市的脾气。Critics characterize the city as restless and young.
sceneCN: 这里 characterize 指「把…描绘成」（第 1 个义项：描述某物具有的特征）；句意是评论家把这座城市描绘成躁动而年轻。

senses.title: To describe the nature of
senses.definition: to describe the typical qualities of a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 描述某人或某物的典型品质
senses.example: Critics characterize the city as restless and young.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家把这座城市描绘成躁动而年轻。
senses.why: The Greek stem meant to stamp a mark, and describing someone is stamping a mark with words.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词干意为压上记号，而描述一个人就是用词语压上记号。

senses.title: To be a typical mark of
senses.definition: to be a quality that marks a person, place or period
senses.definitionCN: 成为标志某人、某地或某时期的品质
senses.example: Long winters characterize the region.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的冬天是该地区的特点。
senses.why: The same stamp can be applied by the thing itself, so the verb also means to be the mark.
senses.whyCN: 同一枚印章也可以由事物自己盖上，于是这个动词也表示「就是那道记号」。

intro.en: Characterize adds the verb ending -ize to the Greek mark that gave character.
intro.cn: characterize 在给出 character 的希腊语记号后加上动词词尾 -ize。

items.en: Kharakter meant an engraved mark.
items.cn: 希腊语 kharakter 意为刻出的记号。

items.en: Character kept the sense of a distinctive sign.
items.cn: 拉丁语 character 保留独特记号的含义。

items.en: Caracteriser named the act of marking out a nature.
items.cn: caracteriser 指标示出某种本性的行为。

items.en: English characterize meant to describe the qualities of something.
items.cn: 英语 characterize 意为描述某物的品质。

items.en: The passive be characterized by now names a defining feature.
items.cn: 被动式 be characterized by 如今指某项决定性特征。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the character stem, while the meaning group lists verbs of describing.
note.cn: 形近组共享 character 词干，近义组列出描述类动词。

entries.definition: the nature of a person
a typical feature
described or marked in the past
to say what someone or something is like
entries.definitionCN: 说出某人或某物的样子

entries.definition: to show a person or thing in a certain way
entries.definitionCN: 以某种方式表现人或事物

entries.definition: to state the exact nature of something

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the mark root, the -ize verb ending and the passive pattern be characterized by.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用记号词根、-ize 动词词尾以及被动句式 be characterized by。

normal.en: Characterize is character plus -ize, so it means to put the mark into words.
normal.cn: characterize 是 character 加 -ize，意思是用词语把记号说出来。

normal.en: Characterize as is the pattern for calling a thing a certain kind.
normal.cn: characterize as 是把某物称作某种样子的句式。

normal.en: Be characterized by reverses the view and names the mark itself.
normal.cn: be characterized by 把视角反过来，直接说出那道记号。

normal.en: Long winters characterize the region is a natural way to state a feature.
normal.cn: 长冬 characterize the region 是陈述特征的自然说法。

normal.en: The third person characterizes simply adds an s before the z sound.
normal.cn: 第三人称 characterizes 只在 z 音前加一个 s。

abstract.en: Picture a critic drawing three quick lines around a city.
abstract.cn: 想象评论家围着城市飞快画了三笔。

abstract.en: Picture a label being stuck on a whole season.
abstract.cn: 想象一张标签被贴在整个季节上。

abstract.en: Picture a portrait that catches one crooked smile.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅肖像只抓住一个歪嘴的笑。

examples.en: The report characterizes the market as unstable.
examples.cn: 报告把市场描绘成不稳定的。

examples.en: Heavy rain characterizes the summer here.
examples.cn: 大雨是这里夏天的特点。

examples.en: Her work is characterized by sharp detail.
examples.cn: 她的作品以细节锐利为特征。

dict_mnemonic.text: characterize 是 character 加 -ize：把一个人的记号用词语盖出来，就是描绘他的特征。

root: 由 character（希腊语 kharakter，刻痕）加动词后缀 -ize 构成，核心是「压上记号」，引申为描述特征或以…为特征。

sensesIntro.en: Stamping a mark with words gives the describing sense, and being the mark itself gives the passive feature sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 用词语压上记号给出描述义，而自身就是那道记号则给出被动特征义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mark pressed onto a person or period.
core.cn: 核心意象：压在人身上或时代上的一个记号。

branches.en: Critics characterize a city by picking a few traits.
branches.cn: 评论家挑出几个特点来描绘一座城市。

branches.en: Long winters mark the whole region.
branches.cn: 漫长的冬天标记出整个地区。

branches.en: Characterize as fits reports and reviews.
branches.cn: characterize as 常见于报告与评论。

branches.en: Active and passive forms share one stamp.
branches.cn: 主动与被动形式共享同一枚印章。

branches.en: Be characterized by names the mark directly.
branches.cn: be characterized by 直接说出那道记号。

intro.en: Characterize combines the character stem with the verb suffix -ize.
intro.cn: characterize 把 character 词干与动词后缀 -ize 结合起来。

latinIntro.en: The stem goes back to Greek kharakter, a mark cut into a surface.
latinIntro.cn: 词干可追溯到希腊语 kharakter，即刻入表面的记号。

items.exampleCN: 这种风格是她作品的特点。

items.example: The age was characterized by speed.
The character of the town changed.

definition_en: to ask a price for goods or services, to accuse someone officially, or to put electrical energy into a battery
core_image: 货物被装上马车，账单也随之压上来
scene: 前台递来一张账单。They charge extra for a room with a view.
sceneCN: 这里 charge 指「收费」（第 1 个义项：为商品或服务索要钱款）；句意是带景观的房间他们要另外收费。

senses.title: To ask for money
senses.definition: to ask a price for goods or services
senses.definitionCN: 为商品或服务索要价款
senses.example: They charge extra for a room with a view.
senses.exampleCN: 带景观的房间他们要另外收费。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to load a cart, and loading a price onto a bill repeats the same image.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为往车上装货，把价钱压到账单上重复了同一意象。

senses.title: To accuse formally
senses.definition: to accuse someone officially of a crime or fault
senses.definitionCN: 正式指控某人犯有罪行或过错
senses.example: The police charged him with theft.
senses.exampleCN: 警方指控他盗窃。
senses.why: Blame too could be loaded onto a person, so the cart metaphor gave the legal sense.
senses.whyCN: 罪责也能被压到一个人身上，于是装车的比喻给出了法律义。

senses.title: To put power into a battery
senses.definition: to put electrical energy into a battery or device
senses.definitionCN: 把电能送入电池或设备
senses.example: Charge the phone before the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 出发前把手机充好电。
senses.why: Electricity is loaded into a cell the way goods were loaded into a cart.
senses.whyCN: 电被装进电池，正如货物曾被装进马车。

intro.en: Charge goes back to a Latin verb for loading a cart, and every sense keeps something being loaded.
intro.cn: charge 可追溯到拉丁语表示装车的动词，每个义项都保留「装载某物」的意象。

items.en: Carricare meant to load a wagon or cart.
items.cn: 拉丁语 carricare 意为往货车或马车上装货。

items.en: Caricare extended the verb to loading in general.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 caricare 把该动词扩展到一般意义的装载。

items.en: Chargier meant to load, burden or entrust.
items.cn: chargier 意为装载、使负担或托付。

items.en: English charge covered loading, burdening and ordering.
items.cn: 英语 charge 涵盖装载、使负担与命令。

items.en: The word gained the senses of a price, a legal accusation and electric power.
items.cn: 该词获得费用、法律指控与电能等义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the charge stem, while the meaning group lists accusing and loading words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 charge 词干，近义组列出指控与装载类词。

entries.definition: a device that puts power into a battery
to release or unload something
more than one charge
to say someone has done wrong
to send someone an invoice
to put goods onto a vehicle

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the loading cart, the phrase in charge of and the battery sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用装货的马车、短语 in charge of 以及电池义。

normal.en: Charge and car share the Latin loading verb, since a cart is what gets loaded.
normal.cn: charge 与 car 共享拉丁语装车动词，因为被装的就是车。

normal.en: In charge of means the duty has been loaded onto you.
normal.cn: in charge of 意为责任被压到了你身上。

normal.en: Charge a fee is loading a price onto the customer.
normal.cn: charge a fee 就是把价钱压到顾客账上。

normal.en: Charge the battery is loading power instead of goods.
normal.cn: charge the battery 是装电而不是装货。

normal.en: Free of charge means no load of cost at all.
normal.cn: free of charge 意为完全不用承担费用的重负。

abstract.en: Picture a cart piled high until the wheels bend.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆车堆得高高的，轮子都压弯了。

abstract.en: Picture a phone plugged in and glowing at the edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一部插着电、边缘发亮的手机。

abstract.en: Picture a guard pointing at a man in a courtroom.
abstract.cn: 想象警卫在法庭上指着一个人。

examples.en: The garage charges too much for repairs.
examples.cn: 这家修车厂收费太高。

examples.en: She was charged with careless driving.
examples.cn: 她被指控粗心驾驶。

examples.en: The nurse in charge of the ward was kind.
examples.cn: 负责病房的护士很和善。

dict_mnemonic.text: charge 与 car 同源：拉丁语原义是往车上装货，装完货就向你收运费。

root: 源自拉丁语 carricare（装车），经晚期拉丁语 caricare 与古法语 chargier 进入英语；由「装载」引申出费用、指控、充电与掌管。

sensesIntro.en: Loading goods gives a price, loading blame gives an accusation, and loading power gives the battery sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 装货给出价钱，装罪责给出指控，装电力给出充电义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: goods piled onto a cart.
core.cn: 核心意象：货物被堆到马车上。

branches.en: A price is a load placed on the buyer.
branches.cn: 价钱是压在买家身上的一笔负担。

branches.en: An accusation loads blame onto a person.
branches.cn: 指控把罪责压到一个人身上。

branches.en: Charging a battery loads it with power.
branches.cn: 给电池充电就是把电装进去。

branches.en: Money and blame are both burdens carried.
branches.cn: 金钱与罪责都是被背负的重担。

branches.en: The cart image survives in price and power.
branches.cn: 马车意象在价钱与电能中存留。

intro.en: Charge keeps the -charg- stem in charger, discharge and chargeable.
intro.cn: charge 在 charger、discharge 与 chargeable 中保留 -charg- 词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin carricare and Late Latin caricare are the loading verbs behind charge.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 carricare 与晚期拉丁语 caricare 是 charge 背后的「装载」动词。

items.meaning: asked a price in the past
items.exampleCN: 他们向我们收了两次钱。

items.meaning: asking a price or storing power

definition_en: kindness shown to others, an organization that helps people in need, or money and goods given to them
core_image: 一只手把面包递到另一只伸出的手里
scene: 教堂门口摆着一只募捐箱。The charity provides meals for homeless families.
sceneCN: 这里 charity 指「慈善机构」（第 2 个义项：从事救济的组织）；句意是这家慈善机构为无家可归的家庭提供餐食。

senses.title: Kindness toward others
senses.definition: kindness and understanding shown to other people
senses.definitionCN: 对他人的善意与体谅
senses.example: She treats everyone with charity.
senses.exampleCN: 她对每个人都心怀善意。
senses.why: Latin caritas meant dearness and Christian love, the warm root of the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 caritas 意为珍爱与基督之爱，是这个词温暖的根。

senses.title: An organization that helps
senses.definition: an organization set up to help people in need
senses.definitionCN: 为帮助困难者而设立的组织
senses.example: The charity provides meals for homeless families.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构为无家可归的家庭提供餐食。
senses.why: A body of people organized for love of neighbours took the name of the love itself.
senses.whyCN: 一群为关爱邻人而组织起来的人，借用了这份关爱本身的名字。

senses.title: Money or aid given
senses.definition: money or goods given to people who need them
senses.definitionCN: 给予困难者的钱款或物品
senses.example: He gave his spare coat to charity.
senses.exampleCN: 他把多余的外套捐给了慈善机构。
senses.why: The abstract love became concrete in the coins and clothes actually handed over.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的仁爱在真正交出的钱币与衣物中变得具体。

intro.en: Charity descends from a Latin word for dearness, which early Christian writers used for love of one's neighbours.
intro.cn: charity 源自拉丁语表示珍爱的词，早期基督教作家用它指对邻人的爱。

items.en: Carus meant dear or precious.
items.cn: 拉丁语 carus 意为珍贵的、亲爱的。

items.en: Caritas meant dearness and, in Christian use, loving kindness.
items.cn: caritas 意为珍爱，在基督教用法中指仁爱。

items.en: Charité carried both love and almsgiving.
items.cn: charité 同时带有爱与施舍之意。

items.en: English charity named Christian love and mercy.
items.cn: 英语 charity 指基督之爱与怜悯。

items.en: The word now also names the groups and gifts that express this love.
items.cn: 如今该词也指表达这份爱的组织与捐赠。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the charitable stem, while the meaning group lists kindness and aid words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 charitable 词干，近义组列出善意与援助类词。

entries.definition: generous in giving help
in a kind and generous way
more than one charity
the quality of being friendly and caring
help given to those in need
money given to a good cause

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the dear root, the charity shop phrase and the gift sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「珍爱」词根、短语 charity shop 以及捐赠义。

normal.en: Charity and cherish both come from a Latin word for something dear.
normal.cn: charity 与 cherish 都来自拉丁语中表示珍贵之物的词。

normal.en: A charity shop turns donated things into money for the poor.
normal.cn: charity shop 把捐赠物变成给穷人的钱。

normal.en: Out of charity means the act comes from kindness, not duty.
normal.cn: out of charity 意为出于善心而非义务。

normal.en: Charity begins at home is the proverb that keeps the word warm.
normal.cn: Charity begins at home 这句谚语让这个词保持温度。

normal.en: The plural charities covers several organizations at once.
normal.cn: 复数 charities 一次指好几家机构。

abstract.en: Picture a hand passing bread through a narrow doorway.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从窄门口递出面包。

abstract.en: Picture a collection box heavy with small coins.
abstract.cn: 想象一只装满零钱的募捐箱。

abstract.en: Picture a shop window full of second-hand coats.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇摆满旧外套的商店橱窗。

examples.en: The concert raised money for local charities.
examples.cn: 音乐会为当地慈善机构筹款。

examples.en: He never speaks of anyone without charity.
examples.cn: 他谈起任何人都带着善意。

examples.en: The old books were sold for charity.
examples.cn: 那些旧书被卖掉用于慈善。

dict_mnemonic.text: charity 与 cherish 同源：心里珍爱一个人，才会伸手施舍，这就是慈善。

root: 源自拉丁语 carus（珍贵的）及其派生 caritas（珍爱、仁爱），经古法语 charité 进入英语；与 cherish 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Dearness becomes Christian love, love becomes an organized body, and the body turns into gifts of money and goods.
sensesIntro.cn: 珍爱变成基督之爱，爱变成有组织的团体，团体再化为钱物捐赠。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: love that reaches out to a neighbour.
core.cn: 核心意象：伸向邻人的那份爱。

branches.en: Treating people with charity is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 以善意待人是最古老的义项。

branches.en: A charity is a body organized around that love.
branches.cn: 慈善机构是围绕这份爱组织起来的团体。

branches.en: Giving to charity turns feeling into goods.
branches.cn: 捐给慈善把情感变成实物。

branches.en: Both senses keep the idea of giving freely.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留自愿给予的意思。

branches.en: Organizations and gifts depend on each other.
branches.cn: 机构与捐赠彼此依存。

intro.en: Charity keeps the car- dear root in charitable and charitably.
intro.cn: charity 在 charitable 与 charitably 中保留 car-「珍爱」词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin carus and caritas are the dear thing and the love that produced charity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 carus 与 caritas 是产出 charity 的「珍贵之物」与「爱」。

items.exampleCN: 两家慈善机构分享了这笔基金。

latinEntries.example: Carus is the root of charity.
latinEntries.exampleCN: carus 是 charity 的词根。

definition_zh: 魅力；吸引力；护身符；使着迷
definition_en: the quality of pleasing and attracting people, a small object worn for luck, or to delight someone greatly
core_image: 一句低唱的咒语让人不由自主地靠近
scene: 老人讲起年轻时的故事，满屋人都安静了。His easy charm made the room fall silent.
sceneCN: 这里 charm 指「魅力」（第 1 个义项：吸引人的力量）；句意是他从容的魅力让满屋人安静下来。

senses.title: The power to please
senses.definition: the quality of pleasing and attracting other people
senses.definitionCN: 讨人喜欢、吸引他人的品质
senses.example: His easy charm made the room fall silent.
senses.exampleCN: 他从容的魅力让满屋人安静下来。
senses.why: A charm was first a sung spell, and the pull of a spell became the pull of a personality.
senses.whyCN: charm 最初是唱出的咒语，咒语的牵引力变成了人格的吸引力。

senses.title: A small lucky object
senses.definition: a small object worn to bring good luck or keep harm away
senses.definitionCN: 佩戴以求好运或驱除伤害的小物件
senses.example: She wore a silver charm on her wrist.
senses.exampleCN: 她手腕上戴着一枚银质护身符。
senses.why: The spell shrank into a small object that was believed to carry its power.
senses.whyCN: 咒语缩小成一件被认为携带其力量的小物件。

senses.title: To delight someone
senses.definition: to please or attract someone strongly
senses.definitionCN: 强烈地取悦或吸引某人
senses.example: The old town charmed every visitor.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老城让每位游客着迷。
senses.why: Bewitching a person with a song became bewitching them with delight.
senses.whyCN: 用歌声迷惑一个人，变成了用愉悦迷住一个人。

intro.en: Charm began as a Latin word for a song, especially a sung spell, and only later meant personal appeal.
intro.cn: charm 起初是拉丁语中「歌」的说法，尤指唱出的咒语，后来才指个人吸引力。

items.en: Carmen meant a song, poem or incantation.
items.cn: 拉丁语 carmen 意为歌、诗或咒语。

items.en: Charme named a magic spell and the words that carried it.
items.cn: charme 指魔法咒语以及承载它的词句。

items.en: English charm first meant an enchantment or a magic formula.
items.cn: 英语 charm 先指魔法或咒文。

items.en: The word extended to a small object worn for luck.
items.cn: 该词扩展到为求好运而佩戴的小物件。

items.en: The word now chiefly means personal attractiveness and the act of delighting.
items.cn: 如今该词主要指个人吸引力与使人愉悦的行为。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the charm stem, while the meaning group lists appeal and magic words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 charm 词干，近义组列出吸引力与魔法类词。

entries.definition: very pleasing and attractive
a person who charms others
without attractiveness
the power to interest people
a quality that draws people near
a small object worn for protection
entries.definitionCN: 为护身而佩戴的小物件

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the song root, the lucky object and the phrase work like a charm.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「歌」词根、幸运物件以及短语 work like a charm。

normal.en: Charm and carol both begin with a Latin song, though only charm kept the magic.
normal.cn: charm 与 carol 都源自拉丁语的歌，但只有 charm 保留了魔法。

normal.en: A good luck charm is a spell shrunk to pocket size.
normal.cn: good luck charm 是缩到口袋大小的咒语。

normal.en: Work like a charm means the method succeeds as if by magic.
normal.cn: work like a charm 意为方法像施了魔法般奏效。

normal.en: Charm the audience shifts the word from object to action.
normal.cn: charm the audience 把这个词从物件转为动作。

normal.en: The adjective charming drops the e and adds -ing.
normal.cn: 形容词 charming 去掉 e 再加 -ing。

abstract.en: Picture an old singer humming a spell over a sleeping child.
abstract.cn: 想象一位老歌者对着熟睡的孩子低唱咒语。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny silver fish swinging on a bracelet.
abstract.cn: 想象一条小银鱼在手链上晃动。

abstract.en: Picture a whole room turning quiet at one voice.
abstract.cn: 想象整个房间因一个声音而安静下来。

examples.en: The village has a charm that cities lose.
examples.cn: 这个村庄有一种城市已经失去的魅力。

examples.en: He kept his mother's charm in his pocket.
examples.cn: 他把母亲的护身符放在口袋里。

examples.en: The children were charmed by the puppet show.
examples.cn: 孩子们被木偶戏迷住了。

dict_mnemonic.text: charm 原义是「歌」：一首咒歌让人着迷，后来就指一个人身上的魅力。

root: 源自拉丁语 carmen（歌、咒语），经古法语 charme 进入英语；由「咒语」引申为护身符、魅力与使人着迷。

sensesIntro.en: A sung spell gives an object its luck, a personality its pull and a verb its power to delight.
sensesIntro.cn: 唱出的咒语给物件以好运，给性格以吸引力，也给动词以使人愉悦的力量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spell that pulls a person closer.
core.cn: 核心意象：把一个人拉近的咒语。

branches.en: Personal charm is the spell without words.
branches.cn: 个人魅力是不用念出的咒语。

branches.en: A charm on a bracelet carries the old magic.
branches.cn: 手链上的护身符携带古老的魔法。

branches.en: To charm is to cast that spell on someone.
branches.cn: 使着迷就是把这道咒语施于人。

branches.en: The noun names the pull, the verb performs it.
branches.cn: 名词指那股牵引力，动词则施展它。

branches.en: Object and action both come from the spell.
branches.cn: 物件与动作都来自那道咒语。

intro.en: Charm forms charming, charmer and charmless with common endings.
intro.cn: charm 借助常见词尾构成 charming、charmer 与 charmless。

latinIntro.en: Latin carmen is the song or spell that stands behind the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 carmen 是英语这个词背后的歌或咒语。

items.example: The charms hung on a chain.
They were charmed by the town.
items.exampleCN: 他们被这座小镇迷住了。

latinEntries.exampleCN: charme 以 charm 进入英语。

definition_en: a drawing that shows information as lines or figures, a detailed map of the sea, or to record how something develops
core_image: 一张画满曲线与刻度的纸
scene: 墙上挂着一张起伏的折线图。The chart shows sales rising since spring.
sceneCN: 这里 chart 指「图表」（第 1 个义项：用线条或图形表示数据）；句意是图表显示销售额自春天以来不断上升。

senses.title: A diagram of data
senses.definition: a drawing that shows information as lines, bars or figures
senses.definitionCN: 用线条、条形或图形展示信息的图
senses.example: The chart shows sales rising since spring.
senses.exampleCN: 图表显示销售额自春天以来不断上升。
senses.why: A written sheet was used to plot numbers, and the sheet gave its name to the picture.
senses.whyCN: 人们用纸页来标画数字，纸页便把名字给了这幅图。

senses.title: A map of the sea
senses.definition: a detailed map of an area of sea and its coasts
senses.definitionCN: 某片海域及其海岸的详细地图
senses.example: The captain studied the chart before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 船长在天黑前研究了海图。
senses.why: The oldest charts were sheets of paper marked with coasts and depths for sailors.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的 chart 就是画着海岸与水深、供水手使用的纸页。

senses.title: To record how something develops
senses.definition: to record or follow the progress of something over time
senses.definitionCN: 记录或跟踪某事物随时间的发展
senses.example: The doctor charted her recovery week by week.
senses.exampleCN: 医生逐周记录她的康复情况。
senses.why: Plotting points on a paper chart became a verb for watching any course.
senses.whyCN: 在纸图上标点，变成了观察任何进程的动词。

intro.en: Chart comes from a Greek word for a sheet of papyrus, which became paper, map and finally diagram.
intro.cn: chart 源自希腊语表示纸莎草纸页的词，后来依次变成纸、地图，最后指图表。

items.en: Chartes meant a sheet of papyrus for writing.
items.cn: 希腊语 chartes 意为供书写的纸莎草纸页。

items.en: Carta meant paper or a written document.
items.cn: 拉丁语 carta 意为纸或书面文件。

items.en: Charte named a document and later a sea map.
items.cn: charte 指文件，后指海图。

items.en: English chart first meant a sea map for navigation.
items.cn: 英语 chart 最初指导航用的海图。

items.en: The word now chiefly means a diagram of information.
items.cn: 如今该词主要指展示信息的图表。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the carta root, while the meaning group lists graphs and maps.
note.cn: 形近组共享 carta 词根，近义组列出图表与地图类词。

entries.definition: a formal document granting rights
recorded or mapped in the past
not yet mapped or explored
a diagram of numerical relations
a simple drawing of how something works
entries.definitionCN: 说明事物如何运作的简图

entries.definition: a drawing of an area of land

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the paper root, the bar chart phrase and the sea map sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「纸」词根、短语 bar chart 以及海图义。

normal.en: Chart, card and charter all come from Latin carta, a sheet of paper.
normal.cn: chart、card 与 charter 都来自拉丁语 carta，即一张纸。

normal.en: A bar chart turns numbers into paper bars you can compare.
normal.cn: bar chart 把数字变成可以比较的纸上长条。

normal.en: A sea chart is the oldest kind, drawn for sailors.
normal.cn: 海图是最古老的一种，为水手而画。

normal.en: To chart progress is to draw the course on paper.
normal.cn: chart progress 就是把进程画在纸上。

normal.en: Off the chart means the value has gone past every marked line.
normal.cn: off the chart 意为数值越过了所有标出的线。

abstract.en: Picture a line climbing steeply across squared paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一条线在方格纸上陡峭上升。

abstract.en: Picture a captain tracing depths with one finger.
abstract.cn: 想象船长用一根手指描着水深。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of weather symbols pinned to a board.
abstract.cn: 想象一墙钉在板上的天气符号。

examples.en: The pie chart divides spending into four parts.
examples.cn: 饼图把开销分成四部分。

examples.en: Sailors once depended on hand-drawn charts.
examples.cn: 水手曾依赖手绘海图。

examples.en: The team charted the river's course last summer.
examples.cn: 团队去年夏天绘制了这条河的走向。

dict_mnemonic.text: chart 与 card 同源：都来自拉丁语「纸」（carta），纸上画满线就成了图表。

root: 源自希腊语 chartes（纸莎草纸页），经拉丁语 carta 与古法语 charte 进入英语；与 card、charter 同源。

sensesIntro.en: A sheet of paper first holds a sea map, then a diagram, and finally the verb of plotting any course.
sensesIntro.cn: 一张纸先承载海图，再承载图表，最后化为标画任何进程的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a marked sheet of paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张画满记号的纸。

branches.en: A bar chart is data drawn on paper.
branches.cn: 条形图是画在纸上的数据。

branches.en: A sea chart guides a ship past hidden rocks.
branches.cn: 海图引导船只避开暗礁。

branches.en: To chart a recovery is to mark each step.
branches.cn: 记录康复就是标出每一步。

branches.en: Both are sheets marked to guide the eye.
branches.cn: 两者都是为引导视线而标记的纸页。

branches.en: The mapped route becomes the recorded course.
branches.cn: 绘出的路线变成被记录的进程。

intro.en: Chart keeps the cart- paper root in uncharted and chartless.
intro.cn: chart 在 uncharted 与 chartless 中保留 cart-「纸」词根。

latinIntro.en: Greek chartes and Latin carta are the papyrus sheet and the paper behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 chartes 与拉丁语 carta 是这个词背后的纸莎草纸页与纸张。

items.example: The chart is out of date.

items.meaning: mapped or recorded in the past

items.exampleCN: 小船进入未标注的水域。
他们没有海图就出航了。

latinEntries.exampleCN: carta 给出 chart 与 charter。

definition_en: a formal document granting rights, a written set of rules for an organization, or to hire a vehicle for private use
core_image: 一张盖着印章、写明权利的羊皮纸
scene: 小镇的档案馆里锁着一份古老文件。The town received its charter in the Middle Ages.
sceneCN: 这里 charter 指「特许状；宪章」（第 1 个义项：授予权利的正式文件）；句意是这座小镇在中世纪获得了特许状。

senses.title: A document granting rights
senses.definition: a formal document that gives rights or privileges to a group or place
senses.definitionCN: 授予某团体或某地权利与特权的正式文件
senses.example: The town received its charter in the Middle Ages.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小镇在中世纪获得了特许状。
senses.why: A small sheet of paper bearing a seal was enough to grant a town its freedoms.
senses.whyCN: 一张盖印的小纸片，就足以授予一座城镇自由。

senses.title: To hire a vehicle privately
senses.definition: to hire a plane, boat or bus for private use
senses.definitionCN: 为私人用途租用飞机、船只或客车
senses.example: They chartered a boat for the afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 他们包了一艘船度过下午。
senses.why: The paper that granted a right became the written contract that granted the use of a vessel.
senses.whyCN: 授予权利的纸，变成了授予船只使用权的书面合同。

senses.title: The rules of an organization
senses.definition: a written statement of the aims and rules of an organization
senses.definitionCN: 说明某组织宗旨与规则的书面文件
senses.example: The club revised its charter last year.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部去年修订了章程。
senses.why: An organization's founding document borrowed the name of the town's founding grant.
senses.whyCN: 组织的创立文件借用了城镇创立特许状的名称。

intro.en: Charter comes from the same Latin paper word as chart, through a small sheet that carried a grant.
intro.cn: charter 与 chart 同出拉丁语「纸」一词，经由承载授权的纸页而来。

items.en: Carta meant paper or a written document.
items.cn: 拉丁语 carta 意为纸或书面文件。

items.en: Chartula was a small sheet used for a legal grant.
items.cn: chartula 指用于法律授权的纸页。

items.en: Chartre named a sealed grant of rights.
items.cn: chartre 指盖印的权利授予书。

items.en: English charter meant a written grant of privileges.
items.cn: 英语 charter 指书面授予的特权。

items.en: The word now also names founding rules and the hiring of a vehicle.
items.cn: 如今该词还指创始章程与交通工具的包租。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the carta root, while the meaning group lists documents and hiring words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 carta 词根，近义组列出文件与租用类词。

entries.definition: a diagram or sea map
officially licensed or hired
a person who hires a ship or plane
the fundamental rules of a state or group
entries.definitionCN: 国家或团体的根本规则

entries.definition: a contract to rent property
to pay to use something

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the paper root, the UN Charter phrase and the chartered flight sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「纸」词根、短语 UN Charter 以及包机义。

normal.en: Charter and chart are siblings from Latin carta, a sheet of paper.
normal.cn: charter 与 chart 是拉丁语 carta（纸页）的兄弟。

normal.en: A charter is a paper that grants, whether rights or a whole boat.
normal.cn: charter 是一张授予东西的纸，授予权利或整艘船都行。

normal.en: The UN Charter is the founding paper of a world body.
normal.cn: the UN Charter 是一个世界组织的创立文件。

normal.en: A charter flight is a plane hired by one group.
normal.cn: charter flight 是一个团体包下的飞机。

normal.en: The verb charter puts the paper into action, as in charter a bus.
normal.cn: 动词 charter 让这张纸动起来，如 charter a bus。

abstract.en: Picture a wax seal pressed onto heavy parchment.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚火漆印章压在厚重的羊皮纸上。

abstract.en: Picture a group boarding a small plane reserved for them.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人登上一架专为他们预留的小飞机。

abstract.en: Picture a museum case holding one yellowed page.
abstract.cn: 想象博物馆展柜里放着一页发黄的纸。

examples.en: The charter protects the rights of the members.
examples.cn: 章程保护成员的权利。

examples.en: They chartered a bus for the school trip.
examples.cn: 他们为学校旅行包了一辆客车。

examples.en: The city was founded by royal charter.
examples.cn: 这座城市依皇家特许状而建立。

dict_mnemonic.text: charter 与 chart 同源：都是纸。写满权利的纸叫宪章，写明租约的纸叫包租。

root: 源自拉丁语 carta（纸、文书）的指小形式 chartula，经古法语 chartre 进入英语；与 chart、card 同源。

sensesIntro.en: A sealed paper grants rights to a town, rules to a body and the private use of a vehicle.
sensesIntro.cn: 一张盖印的纸授予城镇权利、授予团体规则，也授予交通工具的私人使用权。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed paper that grants a right.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张授予权利的盖印纸页。

branches.en: A royal charter grants a town its freedoms.
branches.cn: 皇家特许状授予城镇自由。

branches.en: A charter contract hires a boat for a day.
branches.cn: 包租合同租下一天的船。

branches.en: An organization's charter states its aims.
branches.cn: 组织章程说明其宗旨。

branches.en: Both are founding papers with authority.
branches.cn: 两者都是具有权威的创立文件。

branches.en: The granting paper became the hiring contract.
branches.cn: 授予权利的纸演变为租用合同。

intro.en: Charter keeps the cart- paper root in chartered and charterer.
